reader.requirement: At --std 85 both MOD arguments must be integer arguments (§1989:A.2.2 AR4) and each non-integer argument, in either position, is refused; integer arguments, signed ones included, yield argument-1 - argument-2 * INTEGER(argument-1 / argument-2).

reader.notes: Each MOD position is screened by the same integer screen and refused per position at --std 85 as at 2023; signed integer arguments give the standard's table values and an 18-digit argument is exact. Diagnostics at --std 85 cite §2023:15.64.3 r1.

refuter.evidence: fn_edge.cob at --std 85: COMPUTE RS = FUNCTION MOD(N * (N + 1) / 2 4) refused, 'error COBOL1627: FUNCTION MOD argument-1 is an arithmetic expression whose term (N * (N + 1)) is an integer under the net factor 0.5 ...'; the argument always results in an integer value (product of consecutive integers is even), so §1989:A.2.28.3 AR1 with §1989:A.2.2 AR4 makes it legal. Same at --std 2023. Admitted and correct: MOD(INTEGER-PART(SC) 2) = 0, MOD(K LENGTH(X)) with K = -7 gives 3, MOD(-11 ORD-MIN(9 5 1 7 3)) = 1 (fn_legal2.cob). Refused correctly: MOD(N (1:1) 2) (reference modification is alphanumeric), MOD(NUMVAL("5") 2), MOD(7 FUNCTION RANDOM) (fn_refuse2.cob). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.28.3 AR1 'Argument-1 and argument-2 must be integers'; OK §1989:A.2.2 AR4.
